notes: A special locus inside K3 moduli, not the full K3 family.

repair and reference: Use lattice-polarized K3 deformations/periods, not addition of presumed conditions. Huybrechts (2016 draft), Chapter 6 §2 and Corollary 4.4; see VII bibliography.

repair and reference: H²=4.
notes: Scan confirms F16.

gap or error (if any): Detailed singularity/projective construction not reproduced.

statement (modern): The text reports that these two nodal degree-ten models smooth in a common family.
gap or error (if any): The cited du Val smoothing proof was not checked.
repair and reference: Global primitive polarized moduli irreducibility is verified separately; it does not automatically verify these particular local smoothing claims. Huybrechts (2016 draft), Chapter 6 §2 and Corollary 4.4; see VII bibliography.
notes: Historical assertion kept distinct from modern theorem.

statement (modern): For each fixed primitive positive degree, the complex polarized K3 moduli space is irreducible of dimension nineteen.
gap or error (if any): The printed one-family formulation needs primitive-polarization scope; divisibility cannot change in a smooth polarized family.

notes: Modern verified form of the closing d’Orgeval attribution.

statement (modern): For a minimal regular surface with absolute linear genus one, K²=0.
gap or error (if any): Absolute linear genus is an invariant of the minimal model; blowing up changes K².
repair and reference: Use p^(1)=1+K_min². Dolgachev (1981), Chapter II §1; Schutt and Shioda (2010), §§3–6; see VII bibliography.
notes: This is the convention governing all of §4.

statement (modern): If such a surface has Kodaira dimension one, some positive multiple of K defines a fibration.
gap or error (if any): The source invokes an earlier existence theorem; K²=0 alone does not imply a pencil.
repair and reference: Surface abundance in characteristic zero, followed by Stein factorization.
notes: The K3 case has κ=0 and is expressly exceptional.

statement (modern): A general fibre of the canonical fibration has arithmetic genus one.
repair and reference: Its class F satisfies F²=K·F=0; adjunction gives p_a(F)=1.
notes: Generic smoothness over C gives a smooth genus-one generic fibre.

statement (modern): On a regular surface the base of a connected fibration is P1.
repair and reference: Pullback H1(O_B) injects into H1(O_X), so g(B)≤q(X)=0.
notes: Connected fibres are required; use Stein factorization first.

statement (modern): A nonzero effective pluricanonical divisor on a minimal K²=0 surface has arithmetic genus one.
repair and reference: Adjunction gives 1+((mK)²+mK·K)/2=1.
notes: A reducible or disconnected pluricanonical divisor can still have arithmetic genus one; this does not say each component is an elliptic curve.

statement (modern): Every pluricanonical class has self-intersection zero on the minimal surface.
repair and reference: (mK)²=m²K²=0.
notes: Not generally valid on a nonminimal blow-up.

statement (modern): A complex Enriques surface admits genus-one pencils.
repair and reference: Use nef isotropic half-fibres and |2E|. Cossec, Dolgachev, and Liedtke (2025), Generalities/Linear Systems; see VII bibliography.
notes: Existence is independent of its κ=0 pluricanonical maps.

statement (modern): A K3 surface need not admit a genus-one fibration.
repair and reference: A projective K3 with Picard group generated by a positive-square class has no nonzero isotropic fibre class. Huybrechts (2016 draft), Chapter 6 §2 and Corollary 4.4; see VII bibliography.
notes: The text explicitly reserves the p=P=1 case.

statement (modern): For the regular elliptic surfaces considered, the Zeuthen–Segre invariant is I=12p+8.
gap or error (if any): The invariant and its pencil conventions are imported from earlier chapters.
repair and reference: Noether gives e(X)=12χ=12(p+1); for a genus-one pencil on P1, I=e(X)−4.
notes: Use the minimal smooth relatively minimal model.

statement (modern): The singular-fibre contribution S is 12p+12.
gap or error (if any): S must count total Euler contribution, not merely the number of singular fibre locations.
repair and reference: e(X)=Σ_v e(F_v)=12(p+1). Dolgachev (1981), Chapter II §1; Schutt and Shioda (2010), §§3–6; see VII bibliography.
notes: For a fibration with only I1 fibres it equals the number of nodes/fibres; I_n contributes n.

statement (modern): In the source convention S=I+4.
repair and reference: Combine I=12p+8 with e(X)=S.
notes: The smooth generic fibre has Euler characteristic zero.

statement (modern): The determinant d is the least positive degree of a multisection of the genus-one pencil.
gap or error (if any): Interpret degree after passing to the generic curve over C(t); avoid treating every virtual curve class as an effective irreducible multisection.
repair and reference: The index of the generic genus-one curve is the modern invariant.
notes: Over C(t), period and index agree; the least effective degree is d.

statement (modern): Two genus-one fibrations on the same surface can have different determinants.
repair and reference: The index belongs to a specified fibration, not merely the underlying surface.
notes: Enriques fibrations always have index2; the general definition is broader.

statement (modern): If a multiple fibre is mF0, then m divides the degree of every multisection.
repair and reference: For a horizontal divisor D, D·(mF0)=m(D·F0).
notes: In particular m divides d.

statement (modern): Determinant one gives a section.
repair and reference: A degree-one point on the generic curve is C(t)-rational and its closure is a section of the proper smooth model.
notes: After resolving the rational map to the base, properness extends the generic section.

statement (modern): A genus-one fibration with a section has no multiple fibres.
repair and reference: The section has intersection1 with a full fibre, impossible for mF0 with m>1.
notes: Does not exclude reducible fibres.

statement (modern): A degree-d line bundle on a smooth genus-one curve has d sections when d>0.
repair and reference: Curve RR and h0(L^−1)=0.
notes: This is the fibrewise complete g^(d−1)_d used in the construction.

statement (modern): For d≥3, the complete degree-d system embeds the generic genus-one curve.
repair and reference: A degree≥3 line bundle on a genus-one curve separates all length-two subschemes by RR.
notes: This embedding is over the ground field of the curve.

statement (modern): The degree-two system maps the generic genus-one curve two-to-one to P1 when its target is split.
gap or error (if any): Over a general field the target may initially be a conic; over C(t) it is split.
repair and reference: Tsen’s C1 theorem, or a genuine rank-two pushforward of a line bundle on the surface.
notes: The base field is essential to the plane-double-model reduction.

statement (modern): The fibrewise images for d≥3 sweep a ruled family in a projective bundle over P1.
gap or error (if any): Global generation and the chosen relative system must be arranged by a sufficiently positive base twist.
repair and reference: Use f_*O_X(D) and relative evaluation; twist by O_P1(s).
notes: A ruled family of projective spaces is not automatically a nonsingular scroll in the chosen projective image.

statement (modern): The degree-two construction gives a double cover of a rational ruled surface.
gap or error (if any): It requires a relative complete system, normalization, and resolution of its singularities.
repair and reference: Use the relative degree-two map and the birational rationality of a ruled surface over P1.
notes: Plane branch degree then depends on the chosen birational ruling model.

statement (modern): If d=1 and θ is a section, |3θ| on the generic fibre gives its plane cubic embedding.
repair and reference: The restricted line bundle has degree3 and three sections.
notes: Adding a large multiple of a fibre globalizes this relative cubic map.

statement (modern): The pencils through the image of the section give a degree-two function on each cubic.
repair and reference: On a smooth plane cubic the residual intersections of lines through a fixed point define |2P|.
notes: The resulting global double cover requires contraction/resolution as usual.

statement (modern): For a divisor L of fibre degree d, (L+F)²−L²=2d.
repair and reference: F²=0 and L·F=d.
notes: This is a self-intersection increment, not a dimension increment.

statement (modern): For that divisor, p_a(L+F)−p_a(L)=d.
repair and reference: Adjunction and K·F=F²=0.
notes: Audit derivation; not a separately proved source assertion. This holds for virtual divisors as an intersection identity.

statement (modern): For that divisor, χ(O(L+F))−χ(O(L))=d.
gap or error (if any): The printed assertion that the dimension rises by2d is false in the eventual nonspecial range.
repair and reference: Surface RR: [2L·F+F²−K·F]/2=d.
notes: Audit derivation; not a separately proved source assertion. New definite author slip; see corrections row.

statement (modern): For sufficiently large s, h0(L+(s+1)F)−h0(L+sF)=d.
gap or error (if any): Vanishing must be on the base after pushforward, not presumed from a raw dimension count.
repair and reference: The vector bundle f_*O_X(L) has rank d; twist by O(s), use H1(P1,E(s))=0 eventually.
notes: Audit derivation; not a separately proved source assertion. For d>0 the generic fibre H1 vanishes; torsion higher direct-image terms do not change the eventual rank slope.

statement (modern): Adding fibre divisors preserves the multisection degree.
repair and reference: (L+sF)·F=L·F=d.
notes: This permits positivity while retaining a prescribed relative degree.

statement (modern): Adding enough fibres yields the desired irreducible multisection system in the stated construction.
gap or error (if any): False for the degree-one section class if interpreted literally: |θ+sF| has θ fixed.
repair and reference: Use degree≥2 for a moving relative map, or the stated |3θ+sF| construction in index1.
notes: Bertini requires generation and a map of surface dimension.

statement (modern): Every index-one genus-one surface has a double-plane birational presentation.
gap or error (if any): The argument gives a ruled double cover, then a plane birational model; it does not control the complete singularity list.
repair and reference: Relative |2θ| or Weierstrass x-coordinate, followed by a birational map of the ruled quotient to P2.
notes: Existence of some double plane is distinct from the two restrictive normal forms on p260.

statement (modern): Type I has branch degree2n and a point O of multiplicity2n−3.
repair and reference: Blow up O to obtain F1 with branch S+(3S+2nF).
notes: Here S²=−1 and S·F=1.

statement (modern): Type II adds an ordinary quadruple branch point B and contains the line OB.
repair and reference: Residual branch has degree2n−1, multiplicity2n−4 at O and3 at B.
notes: Generic ordinary tangent directions are needed for the numerical resolution used below.

statement (modern): The printed two-type list exhausts determinant-one minimal plane branch presentations.
gap or error (if any): False as a classification of all index-one elliptic surfaces; generic Weierstrass surfaces avoid the reducible fibres forced by these forms.
repair and reference: Retain these as special plane loci; see the local branch-crossing calculation and Weierstrass dimension below.
notes: High-confidence substantive error, not a simple typo.

statement (modern): For type I the double-cover line bundle on F1 is 2S+nF.
repair and reference: The branch is 4S+2nF, twice that class.
notes: Audit derivation; not a separately proved source assertion. Auditor’s modern reconstruction of the printed invariant calculation.

statement (modern): For type I, K_F1+(2S+nF)=(n−3)F.
notes: Audit derivation; not a separately proved source assertion. All divisor classes are on the blown-up quotient before resolving branch crossings.

statement (modern): The resolved type-I cover has χ(O_X)=n−1.
repair and reference: Double-cover formula χ=2χ(O_F1)+L(L+K_F1)/2=2+(2n−6)/2=n−1.
notes: Audit derivation; not a separately proved source assertion. Ordinary branch nodes give rational double points and do not change χ.

statement (modern): Type I has geometric genus p=n−2.
repair and reference: q=0 and p=χ−1; equivalently h0((n−3)F)=n−2 for n≥3.
notes: For n=2 the rational elliptic case has p=0 but no positive canonical sections; the text assumes P≥1.

statement (modern): Type-I canonical divisors are pullbacks of n−3=p−1 ruling fibres.
repair and reference: Canonical double-cover formula and crepant resolution at the ordinary branch nodes.
notes: The assertion concerns the relatively minimal elliptic model.

statement (modern): For type I and p≥1, P_i=i(p−1)+1.
repair and reference: f_*O_X=O_P1 and K_X=f^*O(p−1).
notes: For p=0 one must use max(0,1−i); the printed range P≥1 excludes that case.

statement (modern): An ordinary quadruple branch point lowers χ of the resolved double cover by1.
repair and reference: A branch multiplicity4 blow-up has a=floor(4/2)=2 and correction a(a−1)/2=1.
notes: Audit derivation; not a separately proved source assertion. Canonical resolution formula; rational double point corrections contribute zero.

statement (modern): Type II has χ(O_X)=n−2.
repair and reference: Apply the multiplicity2n−3 correction at O, then the quadruple-point correction at B.
notes: Audit derivation; not a separately proved source assertion. The extra ordinary branch-node blow-ups have a=1 and leave χ unchanged.

statement (modern): Type II has p=n−3.
repair and reference: q=0, hence p=χ−1=n−3.
notes: The two exceptional contractions do not alter p_g or q.

statement (modern): Before the two final contractions the type-II resolved cover has K²=−2.
repair and reference: After blowing O and B, K_Y+L=(n−3)(H−E_O)−E_B has square−1; double cover multiplies by2.
notes: Audit derivation; not a separately proved source assertion. Further ordinary branch-node resolutions are crepant.

statement (modern): The strict transform ℓ of OB on the resolved quotient has self-intersection−2.
repair and reference: It is H−E_O−E_B−E_1, where E_1 is the blow-up at its branch crossing with E_O.
notes: The scan misnames OB and B as OP and P; additional branch crossings elsewhere must also be resolved.

statement (modern): The ramification curve R above ℓ has self-intersection−1.
repair and reference: π*ℓ=2R and (π*ℓ)²=2ℓ² imply4R²=−4.
notes: Audit derivation; not a separately proved source assertion. It is one ramification component, not two disjoint unramified lifts.

statement (modern): The exceptional curve over B lifts to a genus-one curve V with V²=−2.
repair and reference: Its double cover is branched at four distinct points and the quotient exceptional curve has square−1.
notes: Audit derivation; not a separately proved source assertion. Generic ordinary quadruple-point hypothesis.

statement (modern): The exceptional curve E_1 over the branch crossing lifts to a rational curve W with W²=−2.
repair and reference: The degree-two cover of E_1 is branched at two points.
notes: Audit derivation; not a separately proved source assertion. Ordinary branch-node hypothesis.

statement (modern): The fibre over OB is 2R+V+W.
repair and reference: Pull back the ruling fibre ℓ+E_B+E_1.
notes: Audit derivation; not a separately proved source assertion. Intersections are R·V=R·W=1 and V·W=0.

statement (modern): Contracting R makes W a (−1)-curve.
repair and reference: W² changes from−2 to−2+(W·R)²=−1.
notes: Audit derivation; not a separately proved source assertion. V also then has square−1 but is elliptic, so it is not a Castelnuovo exceptional curve.

statement (modern): Contracting W next makes V a smooth fibre of square zero.
repair and reference: After the first contraction V·W=1; the second raises V² from−1 to0.
notes: Audit derivation; not a separately proved source assertion. These are two successive rational contractions; the footnote’s simultaneous two-(−1)-curve wording needs this interpretation.

statement (modern): The resulting minimal type-II model has K²=0.
repair and reference: Each rational (−1)-curve contraction raises K² by1, so−2+2=0.
notes: Audit derivation; not a separately proved source assertion. All other ordinary branch singularities have already been minimally resolved.

statement (modern): For type II and p≥1, P_i=i(p−1)+1.
repair and reference: After the vertical contractions the relatively minimal elliptic surface has a section and no multiple fibres; apply the canonical formula.
notes: The exceptional branch line belongs to the nonminimal plane description, not the final canonical fibre class.

statement (modern): The two displayed genera define different numerical families for varying n.
repair and reference: p is a birational invariant; models with different p cannot be birational.
notes: Within one p, the two displayed plane loci need not be different connected components of full moduli.

statement (modern): The type-I branch section meets its residual branch in2n−3 points counted with multiplicity.
notes: Audit derivation; not a separately proved source assertion. For a general branch these points are distinct transverse intersections.

statement (modern): Each generic type-I branch crossing produces an I2 fibre after resolving the double cover.
repair and reference: Locally w²=u(u−t) times a unit has an A1 point; its resolution supplies the second component of the nodal fibre.
notes: Audit derivation; not a separately proved source assertion. The other two branch points on the ruling fibre are distinct; this local genericity condition is needed.

statement (modern): Type I generically forces2p+1 reducible I2 fibres.
notes: Audit derivation; not a separately proved source assertion. For p>1 the canonical fibration is unique, so birational change of the plane model cannot erase this intrinsic fibre obstruction.

statement (modern): Each displayed plane family contains continuously many birationally inequivalent surfaces.
gap or error (if any): A parameter count proves this only after controlling automorphisms and fibres of the moduli map.
repair and reference: Use the intrinsic Weierstrass parameters or a generically finite moduli map on an appropriate open locus.
notes: Birational equivalence of minimal κ=1 surfaces preserves their intrinsic Iitaka fibration.

statement (modern): For fixed O, the type-I branch systems have projective dimension8n−3.
notes: Assigned ordinary multiplicity conditions are independent in this plane vector space.

statement (modern): The projective stabilizer of a fixed point of P2 has dimension6.
repair and reference: PGL3 has dimension8 and acts transitively on P2 of dimension2.
notes: Generic finite stabilizer of the particular branch is still needed for the quotient count.

statement (modern): The type-I quotient count is8n−9=8p+7.
repair and reference: Subtract6 and substitute p=n−2.
notes: Dimension of this branch-model locus under generic stabilizer assumptions; not all Jacobian surfaces.

statement (modern): The type-II branch family has the printed projective dimension8n−13.
gap or error (if any): Independence of the tacit incidence conditions and treatment of moving B are not established in the text.
repair and reference: Use the plane coefficients with the stated singularity and fixed-line conditions; retain as the indicated generic-locus count.
notes: The later subtraction uses the indicated birational transformation group.

statement (modern): The type-II quotient count is8n−19=8p+5.
gap or error (if any): Requires the stated six-dimensional equivalence group and generic finite fibres of the parameter map.
repair and reference: Subtract6 and use p=n−3.
notes: It is not the dimension of the entire determinant-one moduli space.

statement (modern): The earlier lower bound quoted by the source is M≥9p−2p^(1)+12.
gap or error (if any): The hypotheses of the earlier theorem are not reproduced here.
repair and reference: Do not apply a bound for full deformation families to arbitrary special plane subloci.
notes: In the present p^(1)=1 case the bound reads9p+10.

statement (modern): For p^(1)=1 the quoted lower bound becomes9p+10.

statement (modern): The type-I and type-II counts are smaller than9p+10 in the stated nonnegative-p range.

notes: This flags special subloci; it does not establish their claimed completeness.

statement (modern): Index-one surfaces can occur as specializations inside families whose generic index is2.
gap or error (if any): Index can decrease under specialization; this does not show every Jacobian surface belongs to the two chosen branch loci.
repair and reference: Track the appearance of a section in a genus-one torsor family.
notes: The source’s proposed explanation is plausible only with an actual family and specialization analysis.

statement (modern): Type I′ has branch degree2n and multiplicity2n−4 at O.
repair and reference: On F1 its branch class is4S+2nF, without S as a compulsory component.
notes: The generic cover has relative degree-two polarization and often index2.

statement (modern): Type I′ has p=n−2.
repair and reference: Double-cover χ=n−1, hence p=χ−1.
notes: Ordinary branch and regularity assumptions.

statement (modern): The type-I′ parameter count is10n−12=10p+8.
repair and reference: Projective coefficient dimension10n−6 minus the6-dimensional fixed-point stabilizer.
notes: Generic smooth branch on the ruled model and finite stabilizer assumed.

statement (modern): A degree-two ruled double-cover presentation only proves that the generic index divides2.
gap or error (if any): It does not prove every member has index exactly2.
repair and reference: The ruling’s pullback supplies a degree-two divisor; special members can acquire a section.
notes: Audit derivation; not a separately proved source assertion. Correct scope of the determinant2 label for the enlarged branch families.

statement (modern): The parameter count for a general Jacobian elliptic surface over P1 with χ=p+1 is10p+8.

statement (modern): For general multiplicities, P_m=max(0,1+m(p−1)+Σ_j floor(m(m_j−1)/m_j)).

notes: Audit derivation; not a separately proved source assertion. A modern complete formula replacing the abbreviated generalization; char0 relatively minimal setting.

statement (modern): The genus p and the multiplicity list determine this plurigenus sequence.

statement (modern): The associated Jacobian fibration is formed by Pic0 of the smooth generic genus-one curve.

notes: A zero section is built into the Jacobian.

statement (modern): The Jacobian has determinant one.
repair and reference: Its zero section has degree1.
notes: It therefore has no multiple fibres in characteristic zero.

statement (modern): A genus-one curve and its Jacobian are isomorphic over an algebraic closure.
repair and reference: Choose a geometric point and send x to[x−P].
notes: Over C(t) such an isomorphism requires a rational point or a trivial torsor; do not infer it from equal j-invariant.

statement (modern): A degree-d line bundle defined over C(t) identifies Pic^d(C) with Pic0(C).
repair and reference: Translation by that line bundle is an isomorphism of Picard torsors.
notes: A degree-d divisor class defined only geometrically is insufficient.

statement (modern): A degree-d effective multisection divisor supplies such a rational Pic^d point.
repair and reference: Restrict its line bundle to the generic fibre.
notes: Use a genuine divisor on the surface; descent of an arbitrary invariant geometric class can have a Brauer obstruction.

statement (modern): The source proposes a correspondence of type[d,d] between the original and Jacobian surfaces.
gap or error (if any): Its varying choice of effective representatives is not justified; descent and extension across singular fibres need formulation.
repair and reference: Auditor construction: fix P1+...+Pd over a splitting field and take the Galois-invariant union of graphs x↦[x−Pi].
notes: This gives a correspondence rather than an isomorphism of the generic torsor and its Jacobian.

statement (modern): That graph-union construction has degree d over each generic curve.
repair and reference: Each of the d graphs is an isomorphism geometrically; counting with multiplicity gives degree d on each projection.
notes: Audit derivation; not a separately proved source assertion. Use a separable multisection and retain multiplicities if translated graphs coincide.

statement (modern): The graph union descends to the base field.
repair and reference: Galois permutes the Pi and hence the graph components, so the cycle is invariant and descends.
notes: Audit derivation; not a separately proved source assertion. The construction is the auditor’s modern replacement, not an attributed historical repair.

statement (modern): Taking its closure gives an algebraic correspondence between smooth projective surface models.
repair and reference: Proper closure in X×_B J and resolution if necessary.
notes: Audit derivation; not a separately proved source assertion. Boundary components can appear over singular fibres and must not be mistaken for generic degree changes.

statement (modern): A genus-one fibration and its Jacobian have the same χ(O).
repair and reference: Their fundamental line bundles and Euler contributions agree in characteristic zero. Dolgachev (1981), Chapter II §1; Schutt and Shioda (2010), §§3–6; see VII bibliography.
notes: Local Jacobian comparison and the canonical bundle formula supply the modern theorem.

statement (modern): For regular original and Jacobian surfaces, equality of χ gives equality of p_g.
repair and reference: q=0 on both and p_g=χ−1.
notes: Do not infer this when irregularity has not been controlled.

statement (modern): Nonmultiple local fibres of a genus-one fibration are compared with the corresponding Jacobian fibres.
gap or error (if any): A global isomorphism need not exist; formulate the comparison after suitable local base change.
repair and reference: Use the local structure theorem for genus-one torsors over a strictly henselian DVR. Dolgachev (1981), Chapter II §1; Schutt and Shioda (2010), §§3–6; see VII bibliography.
notes: The theorem, not an arbitrary coordinate identification, controls the singular-fibre type.

statement (modern): A multiple fibre and the corresponding Jacobian fibre have the same Euler contribution after accounting for the reduced fibre.
repair and reference: In characteristic zero the allowed multiple fibres are smooth or of multiplicative type; mI_b has reduced fibre I_b with Euler b. Dolgachev (1981), Chapter II §1; Schutt and Shioda (2010), §§3–6; see VII bibliography.
notes: Nilpotent multiplicity does not change the underlying topological Euler characteristic.

statement (modern): For a genus-one fibration with χ>0, q(X)=g(B).
repair and reference: Leray and relative duality give R1f_*O_X=L^−1 of negative degree, hence no global sections; H1(O_X)=H1(O_B).
notes: Characteristic zero and relatively minimal connected fibration; wild-fibre torsion is absent.

statement (modern): Consequently the base genus is p_g−p_a(X).
repair and reference: p_a=χ−1=p_g−q, so q=p_g−p_a.

statement (modern): The case p_a(X)=−1 is χ(O_X)=0.

notes: The positive-χ proof cannot simply be reused.

statement (modern): An abelian surface has q=2,p_g=1 and χ=0.

notes: The existence of an elliptic fibration requires an elliptic quotient; not every simple abelian surface has one.

statement (modern): A bielliptic surface has q=1,p_g=0 and χ=0.
repair and reference: Modern classification of smooth minimal κ=0 complex surfaces.

statement (modern): Products E×B with g(B)≥2 have K²=0,χ=0,q=g(B)+1,p_g=g(B).

repair and reference: Use this dictionary throughout.
